draft.headline: NQ falls 2.7% as tech earnings and AI spending worries hit
draft.summary: Nasdaq 100 futures dropped 2.74% while S&P futures fell only 0.84%, so the selling was concentrated in tech. Weak Amazon and Intel earnings headlines are the clearest candidates, though some landed right at the end of the move.
draft.what_it_means: Amazon missed on earnings and held capital spending (capex — money spent on things like data centres and chips) steady, which added to worries about AI spending. Intel plunged 20% after blaming a PC slowdown for weak guidance, and a downgrade of Alphabet followed a rough quarter. All three are large Nasdaq names, so trouble there drags the index. Caveat: the Amazon and Intel headlines printed at 16:05–16:11 ET, at or just after the end of the measured window, so the exact trigger is not pinned down.
draft.market_reaction: NQ fell 2.74% today to 29,157.25, including 1.03% between 15:01 and 16:06 ET. S&P 500 futures lost 0.84% today and only 0.22% in that same window, so tech took the damage. The session range of 646 points (2.22%) was 133% of a typical day. VIX rose 1.71% to 17.20.
draft.rates_read: The 10-year yield fell 10.0bp to 4.945% and the 2-year fell 12.4bp to 4.611%; in the move window they slipped 3.7bp and 4.8bp. Falling yields usually help Nasdaq stocks, yet NQ fell hard — so this was not a rates-driven selloff. The tech fear gauge VXN at 23.76 sits 6.56 points above VIX.

draft.learn: Capital spending, or capex, is the money a company puts into long-term assets like data centres and chips. When a giant like Amazon holds capex steady instead of raising it, suppliers expect fewer orders — which is why AI-spending jitters can hit chip and tech stocks fast.
